note: The occupations of the First World War, read by build-eras.mjs (csOccupy). An area is the occupier's side of a front; each point is [longitude, latitude, the place it stands for].

zones.name: General Government of Belgium
zones.wiki: German occupation of Belgium during World War I
zones.note: The General Government covered most of Belgium; Flanders behind the front was under the army (the Etappengebiet), here drawn with it.

zones.name: Occupied France
zones.wiki: German occupation of north-east France during World War I

zones.name: Occupied Luxembourg
zones.wiki: German occupation of Luxembourg during World War I

zones.name: Ober Ost
zones.note: Held to the armistice, and in Belarus until the Red Army entered Minsk (10 December 1918); the Baltic states and Poland are CShapes' own from November 1918.

zones.name: Military Government of Lublin
zones.note: Set up on 25 August 1915 as the General Government of Kielce, it moved to Lublin on 1 October 1915.

zones.name: Ukraine
zones.note: The Ukrainian People's Republic and, from 29 April 1918, the Ukrainian State (the Hetmanate), under German and Austro-Hungarian occupation until the Hetmanate fell (14 December 1918).

zones.name: Lithuania
zones.note: CShapes counts Lithuania independent from its declaration of 16 February 1918; it stayed under German occupation until the armistice.

zones.name: General Government of Galicia and Bukovina
zones.wiki: General Government of Galicia and Bukovina

zones.name: Occupied Dobruja
zones.note: Southern Dobruja was occupied by Bulgaria, the north by Germany and Bulgaria together; the Treaty of Bucharest (May 1918) gave the south to Bulgaria, as CShapes has it from 7 May 1918.

zones.name: Italian-occupied Trentino and Venezia Giulia
zones.wiki: Allied occupation of the eastern Adriatic
zones.note: Until the Treaty of Saint-Germain, from whose coming into force (CShapes: 10 September 1919) the land is Italy's.

zones.name: Italian-occupied Dalmatia
zones.wiki: Allied occupation of the eastern Adriatic

zones.name: Bulgarian-occupied Serbia
zones.wiki: Bulgarian occupation of Serbia (World War I)
zones.note: The Military Inspection Areas of Morava (Niš) and Macedonia (Skopje).

zones.name: French-occupied Alsace-Lorraine
zones.note: French troops entered Mulhouse on 17 November, Metz on 19 November, and Strasbourg on 22 November 1918; the land was ceded by the Treaty of Versailles.

zones.name: Territory of the Saar Basin
zones.note: Governed for the League of Nations from the Treaty of Versailles's coming into force (10 January 1920) until it returned to Germany after the plebiscite of 13 January 1935, on 1 March 1935. Before, French troops held it with the Rhineland.

zones.name: Occupied Rhineland
zones.note: Held by Belgian, British, American, and French troops, drawn here under France, which held the largest zone and the High Commission's chair.

rest.note: CShapes counts all of Serbia occupied by Austria-Hungary from 2 October 1915; the zones above hold what was occupied, and the rest (before the conquest was complete, round Bitola from November 1916, and as it was freed in 1918) is Serbia's.
CShapes counts Montenegro occupied from 2 July 1915; it was conquered in January 1916 and freed in November 1918.

west-1914-08.note: Belgium east of the line from Antwerp to the French border, which the Germans held from the fall of Brussels (20 August 1914) until Antwerp fell; in France, the land behind the German front of 5 September 1914 at the Marne.
ring: Dutch border north of Antwerp's forts

west-1914-09.note: After the Battle of the Marne (to 13 September 1914): France behind the Aisne front, the race to the sea not yet run; Belgium east of Antwerp's line as before.
ring: Dutch border north of Antwerp's forts

west-1914-10.note: After Antwerp fell (10 October 1914): all of Belgium but the corner west of the Yser and Ypres; France as before.

west-1915.note: The Western Front from the end of the race to the sea (November 1914) to the withdrawal to the Hindenburg Line (March 1917), with the Ypres salient of after May 1915.

west-1917.note: The Hindenburg Line, from the German withdrawal (16 March 1917) to the Spring Offensive, with the Allied gains of 1917 at Arras and Vimy (April), Messines (June), Passchendaele (November), and the Chemin des Dames (to the Ailette, October).
ring: east of Vimy Ridge, taken April 1917

west-1918-03.note: After the German offensives of March and April 1918 (Michael and the Lys): the bulge towards Amiens and Montdidier, and Kemmel and Merville in Flanders.

west-1918-05.note: The furthest German advance, after the offensives on the Aisne (27 May 1918) and the Matz (June), to the Allied counterattack of 18 July 1918.

west-1918-07.note: After the Second Battle of the Marne (18 July to 6 August 1918): back to the Vesle; the bulge towards Amiens still German.

west-1918-08.note: After Amiens (8 August) and the advance to the Hindenburg Line (to 25 September 1918): Flanders retaken to Kemmel, the Somme bulge gone, and the Saint-Mihiel salient cut off (12 to 15 September).

west-1918-09.note: After the breaking of the Hindenburg Line and the Meuse-Argonne offensive (26 September to 16 October 1918): Passchendaele, Roulers, Cambrai, Saint-Quentin, and Laon taken.

west-1918-10.note: From the freeing of Lille, Douai, and the Belgian coast (17 to 19 October 1918) to the armistice of 11 November 1918, as the line stood on the 11th: Ghent, Mons, Charleville, and Sedan reached.

west-liege.note: The land east of the Meuse round Liège, held from the fall of the city (7 August 1914) to the fall of Brussels.

alsace-french.note: The French-held corner of Upper Alsace, from Thann and Masevaux to Dannemarie, west of the Vosges front.

all.note: Every land: the whole of the occupied state.

wallachia-1916-11.note: Oltenia, west of the Olt, from the fall of Craiova (21 November 1916).

wallachia-1916-12.note: Wallachia to Buzău, from the fall of Bucharest (6 December 1916).

wallachia-1917.note: The Siret line, from the fall of Focșani (8 January 1917) to the German withdrawal (November 1918).

dobruja-1916-09.note: Southern Dobruja to the Rasova–Tuzla line, from the fall of Turtucaia (6 September 1916).

dobruja-1916-10.note: Dobruja south of the Hârșova line, from the fall of Constanța (22 October 1916).

dobruja-1917.note: All of Dobruja, to the Danube's St George branch, from January 1917.

transylvania-1916.note: The east of Transylvania held by Romania after its invasion (28 August 1916) until it was driven back (October 1916).

isonzo-1915.note: The Austrian land the Italians held from their first advance (May and June 1915) to the fall of Gorizia: the upper Isonzo at Caporetto and Krn, Cormons, Gradisca, Cervignano, and Monfalcone.

isonzo-1916.note: From the fall of Gorizia (8 August 1916) to Caporetto (October 1917).

veneto-1917-10.note: The land the Austro-Hungarian and German armies took after Caporetto, to the Tagliamento (by 3 November 1917).

veneto-1917-11.note: The Austro-Hungarian side of the Piave and Grappa line, from 10 November 1917 to the Battle of Vittorio Veneto.

italy-1918.note: The land Italy held under the armistice of Villa Giusti (4 November 1918): Trentino and South Tyrol to the Brenner, Gorizia, Trieste, and Istria.

dalmatia-1918.note: Northern Dalmatia, held by Italy under the armistice: Zadar, Šibenik, and the islands.

serbia-bg.note: The Bulgarian zone of occupied Serbia: the Morava inspection area (Niš, Pirot, Zaječar, Leskovac, Vranje) and Macedonia (Skopje, Bitola).

serbia-ah.note: The Austro-Hungarian zone of occupied Serbia (the Military General Governorate).

bitola.note: The land round Bitola (Monastir) retaken by the Allies (19 November 1916) and held until the breakthrough of September 1918.

serbia-belgrade-1915.note: The north of Serbia taken by the Austro-Hungarian and German armies in October 1915, before the Bulgarian advance met them.

serbia-1918-09.note: Serbia still held after the Allied breakthrough at Dobro Pole, as on 25 September 1918.

serbia-1918-10.note: Serbia still held after the Bulgarian armistice, as the Allies reached Vranje (5 October 1918).

serbia-1918-10b.note: Serbia still held after Niš was freed (12 October 1918), to the freeing of Belgrade (1 November).

serbia-bg-1916.note: The Bulgarian zone, less the land round Bitola.

serbia-bg-1918-09.note: The Bulgarian zone as held on 25 September 1918.

serbia-ah-1918-10.note: The Austro-Hungarian zone as held in early October 1918.

serbia-ah-1918-10b.note: The Austro-Hungarian zone as held from Niš's freeing to Belgrade's.

korce.note: The French zone round Korçë (the Autonomous Province of Korçë).

albania-north.note: Albania north of the Vjosa, held by Austria-Hungary from January 1916 to October 1918.

albania-south-it.note: Italian Albania south of the Vjosa, less Korçë.

vlore.note: Vlorë and its bay, held by Italy from 26 December 1914.

albania-it-1918.note: Albania less Korçë, held by Italy after the Austro-Hungarian withdrawal (October 1918).

epirus.note: Northern Epirus, held by Greece from October 1914 to 1916: Gjirokastër, Sarandë, and Korçë.

greece-bg.note: Greek Macedonia east of the Struma, held by Bulgaria from August 1916 (Kavala, 12 September) to the armistice.

meso-1914.note: Basra and the Shatt al-Arab, from the taking of Basra (22 November 1914) and Qurna (9 December).

meso-1915-09.note: Kut (29 September 1915), held until its surrender (29 April 1916).

meso-1916.note: After Kut's surrender (29 April 1916): the British line at Sannaiyat and Falahiya, east of Kut.

meso-1917-11.note: Tikrit (6 November 1917), Kifri, and in March 1918 Khan al-Baghdadi.

meso-1918-11.note: All of Mesopotamia with the vilayet of Mosul (Mosul occupied 10 November 1918), until the Mandate.

pal-1917-02.note: The south of Gaza's district, from Rafa (9 January 1917) and Khan Yunis.

pal-1918-02.note: Jericho and the Jordan (21 February 1918), to the Battle of Megiddo.

pal-1918-09.note: After Megiddo (19 September 1918): Palestine, Haifa, Amman, and Deraa.

pal-1918-10c.note: Aleppo (26 October 1918) and the armistice line of Mudros, until the Mandates.

oeta-west.note: The coast of Lebanon and Syria, under French administration (OETA West) from October 1918.

oeta-west-1918-10b.note: OETA West as held in October 1918.

sinai-1914.note: The Sinai east of the Canal's defences, held by Ottoman forces from December 1914 until the British advance of 1916.
ring: the coast east of Port Said

sinai-1916-08.note: After Romani (4 August 1916), the British advance to Bir el Abd and Mazar.

sinai-1916-12.note: After El Arish (21 December 1916), to Rafa (9 January 1917).

cauc-1914.note: The strip by the Russian border held by Russia from the Bergmann offensive (November 1914): Eleşkirt, Karaköse, and Doğubayazıt.

cauc-1915.note: With Van, held by Russian and Armenian forces from 17 May to 4 August 1915.

cauc-1916-02.note: Erzurum (16 February 1916), Muş, Bitlis, and Rize.

cauc-1916-07.note: Erzincan (25 July 1916) and Bayburt, to the Russian collapse of 1918.

cauc-1918-03.note: Van and the border strip, after Erzurum was retaken (12 March 1918), until Van fell (6 April 1918).

straits.note: Constantinople and the Straits, occupied by the Allies from 13 November 1918 to 4 October 1923.

alsace-lorraine.note: Alsace-Lorraine: the German Empire's land in Natural Earth's départements of Moselle, Bas-Rhin, and Haut-Rhin, in the French départements beside them, and in two boxes over its borders with Luxembourg and Switzerland, so that the slivers where CShapes' border of 1871 and Natural Earth's differ go with it.

rhineland-n.note: The northern (Cologne) zone, with its bridgehead, held by British and Belgian troops until 31 January 1926.

rhineland-m.note: The middle (Koblenz) zone, with its bridgehead, held by American and then French troops until 30 November 1929.
ring: in Luxembourg, west of the Sauer
west of the Our, in Luxembourg

rhineland-s.note: The southern (Mainz) zone, with its bridgehead and the Palatinate, held by French troops until 30 June 1930. It runs to the French border: the Saar was occupied with it until the Territory of the Saar Basin, which comes first, took it from 10 January 1920.
ring: the French border, the Saar included

saar-basin.note: The Territory of the Saar Basin under Article 48 of the Treaty of Versailles: Natural Earth's Saarland, with a strip over its French border for the slivers where CShapes' line differs, less the land north of the treaty's line (Perl, Britten, Losheim, Wadern, Weiskirchen, Nonnweiler, Nohfelden, Freisen, and Leitersweiler, which joined in 1946 and 1947), the line drawn by hand from the treaty's description, to some 2 km.
minus: the French border west of Merzig
north of the cantons of Merzig and Haustedt
the line of the Kreise of Saarlouis, Ottweiler, and St. Wendel
